account:
Today my appointments are keeping me moving between the office, mill, home, and later the neighbour's cottage. I reached the mill late after settling arrangements with the innkeeper. I inspected the mill stall and found 74 hay bales; that shows stock is available, but is not a full account of the mill's grain or proof that there are no shortages. I have now arrived home for lunch and have council letters at 13:00, tea at the neighbour's cottage at 15:00, and office time at 16:30.

The unusual thing is the repeated, vague talk of a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery. Townsfolk named the baker, innkeeper, freight, and neighbour as people present in various reports. One also reported the baker carrying a sack of bread, which could simply be normal business. Nobody has explained what the supposed change actually is. The neighbour says they too have only heard vague reports and suggests asking the baker. I crossed the bridge this morning, and I have no firsthand evidence of a crossing problem or an actual change. I should ask the baker directly rather than turn these rumours into facts.

There is also a carefully arranged evening gathering: the innkeeper, secretary, and builder are to meet me at the office at 17:30 and accompany me to the great hall at 18:00. The stated purpose is the lighting inspection, covering eight lanterns and the four tables. The appointment addendum records this as an addition I approved yesterday. The innkeeper was particularly concerned to confirm the escort and timing. It may be nothing more than organising that inspection, although the coordination stands out alongside my feeling that town business is happening without me. I have no evidence linking that gathering to the bakery reports or establishing any hidden purpose.
